items.title: OD1: 150 days - and the legal calendar is now officially inside it
items.summary: Two live legal clocks now sit inside your decision window. The Federal Court hearing runs 25-29 January, and the Budget lands 9 October. The window itself did not change: 150 days to 1 March 2027. What changed this week is that the January dates stopped being an estimate and became a court order.
items.source: Days computed from 2026-10-02; hearing dates per Federal Court direction hearing 1 Oct (Bernama via Malay Mail)

items.title: WALL SETTLED: the court fixed it - five days, 25-29 January
items.summary: Justice Rhodzariah Bujang fixed five hearing days, 25 to 29 January 2027, for the Petronas and Sarawak petitions. Written submissions are due 11 January, replies 18 January, case management 12 January. The petitions are heard separately, in the order filed - Petronas first (filed 10 Jan, leave granted 16 March). Both sides will ask the Chief Justice for an enlarged nine- or eleven-member panel. The anti-thesis search for a postponement returned nothing: this date is fixed on the record.
items.source: Bernama via Malay Mail 1 Oct 2026; FMT/Star/Borneo Post 24 Sep 2026 for the separate-hearings posture. W=2 (Bernama-wire + FMT reporting)

items.title: The 1954 boundaries order becomes the front door to the whole dispute
items.summary: Sarawak will file, within 14 days of 1 October, a preliminary challenge to the validity of the Sarawak (Alteration of Boundaries) Order in Council 1954 - the instrument that fixed its territorial waters. Petronas argues the issue needs no preliminary hearing and belongs inside the main petition. The hearing panel, not this judge, will decide. This is the jurisdictional question that shadows the Bintulu LNG contest, now with its own court date.
items.source: Malay Mail/Bernama 1 Oct 2026 (Rule 23 application, Federal Court Rules 1995); Sarawak petition of 23 Feb seeking to void PDA 1974, Continental Shelf Act 1966 and Petroleum Mining Act 1966 as applied to Sarawak

items.title: Budget 2027: seven days out
items.summary: Budget 2027 is tabled Friday 9 October, confirmed in the Finance Ministry's pre-budget statement. The Economy Minister has already said higher oil prices will not cut development spending. What matters for you is the assumption underneath that sentence, and that lands on the day.
items.source: MOF pre-budget statement (mof.gov.my); Newswav/Economy Minister remarks. W=2 (primary + press)

items.title: WALL MOVED but unresolved: the oil assumption - press says about USD 90, the banks say 64 to 75
items.summary: New Straits Times reported 10 September that Government will likely assume around USD 90 a barrel for 2027, given the Middle East. The banks forecast the opposite direction: EIA sees Brent averaging USD 74 in 2027, JPMorgan cut its call to USD 64, ABN AMRO ends 2027 at USD 70. At roughly RM 300 million of revenue per dollar of Brent, the gap between the budget assumption and the street forecast is measured in billions. The official number stays UNRESOLVED until budget day - the press figure is an estimate, not a filing.
items.source: NST 10 Sep 2026 (press estimate); EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook; JPMorgan note via Reuters-reported coverage; ABN AMRO research. Official assumption: not published. Claim on the RM 300m sensitivity carried from earlier edition, still OPEN

items.title: Brent eased to about USD 97 with the strait still shut
items.summary: Brent fell to USD 96.76 on 1 October, down 1.3 percent on the day but up over 50 percent year on year. A Hormuz tracker records the strait as effectively closed to commercial shipping as of 1 October - day 214 - with one transit on 27 September against a normal of about 85 a day. The market is holding a risk premium on a waterway that is not moving.
items.source: TradingEconomics Brent CFD reading 1 Oct 2026 (W=1, market data); straits.live transit tracker (W=1, tracker); premium-level context per Wikipedia crisis timeline

items.title: Hormuz: the reopening is still a promise, not a schedule
items.summary: Foreign Minister Araghchi said on 25 September that reopening depends on the United States. Since then: no transit recovery, no compliance milestone met. The seven-day phased timetable recorded in the last edition has gained no visible execution. Keep treating the premium as structural until tankers actually sail.
items.source: Wikipedia crisis timeline citing Araghchi 25 Sep; straits.live tracker 1 Oct; chronological lock holds (statement precedes today's still-closed status)

items.title: New pump band: BUDI95 holds at RM 1.99, open-market prices slip a few sen
items.summary: For 1-7 October: RON95 under BUDI95 stays RM 1.99. The unsubsidised RON95 is RM 4.52 (down 5 sen), RON97 RM 5.00 (down 5 sen), diesel RM 5.27 (down 15 sen) in the Peninsula. The state is still paying RM 2.53 a litre - 56 percent of the pump price - on every subsidised litre. The subsidy arithmetic enters Budget 2027 in seven days.
items.source: paultan.org weekly band 1-7 Oct; Time News citing subsidy per litre. W=2

items.title: 91 days until the household threshold drops back to 600 kWh
items.summary: The threshold reverts on 1 January. Above 600 kWh a month, the adjusted fuel cost mechanism starts biting the household bill again. Coal at around USD 148 a tonne remains the input being absorbed. Ninety-one days is one school holiday and one budget away.
items.source: Carried item; day count from 2026-10-02; coal input per earlier edition ledger, still OPEN

items.title: Haze: Kedah still clear - the weather risk this week is thunderstorms, not smoke
items.summary: No haze deterioration found for Kedah; the Sarawak unhealthy readings from last week stand with no new spread reported. The active warning is the monsoon-transition kind: thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds across KL and ten states on 1 October. Nothing that touches the family.
items.source: MetMalaysia warning 1 Oct via Malay Mail; no new API warnings surfaced in sweep. W=1 (MetMalaysia primary)

items.title: The hearing now sits inside the election window - for certain
items.summary: The Sarawak assembly dissolves no later than 14 February 2027; the premier can go earlier, with talk of a poll before December. The 25-29 January hearing therefore sits inside a campaign season either way - the state's counsel walks into court as a candidate, not just a litigant. That shapes tone and settlement appetite more than it shapes the law.
items.source: Sarawak constitution auto-dissolution 14 Feb 2027 (Wikipedia/assembly term); hearing dates 1 Oct court order; no election date announced (UKAS)

items.title: Still open: check the EPF nomination once before OD1
items.summary: Unchanged and still the cheapest insurance you own. Nomination lapses and scheme changes took effect from January 2026; a stale nomination sends savings into intestacy. One check, one sitting.
items.source: EPF policy enhancements effective 1 Jan 2026 (KWSP announcement); carried item, unchanged

items.summary: The 26 September pairing came and went. Retired from the register with a clean settlement: the event date elapsed.

items.title: Two meteor showers this month - one from Halley's own dust
items.summary: The Draconids peak 8-9 October, usually a quiet handful per hour, shed by comet 21P/Giacobini-Zinner. The Orionids peak 21-22 October, up to 20 an hour, from dust trail of comet 1P/Halley - the same comet that visits every 76 years. You are sleeping under its litter. Both peak nights have a waxing-to-new moon window, which favours Kedah skies.
items.source: timeanddate.com October 2026 sky guide; Natural History Museum and EarthSky shower calendars

items.title: Paint that gets colder than the air around it
items.summary: Passive radiative cooling materials made the World Economic Forum's top-ten emerging technologies of 2026: engineered surfaces that dump heat straight to deep space through the atmospheric infrared window and come to rest below ambient temperature, using zero electricity. For a hot, grid-stressed country it reads like science fiction with a paint roller.
items.source: WEF/SOCI Top 10 Emerging Technologies 2026 report listing
